item.title: Higher-dimensional black holes hide an exact symmetry in their ringing, and string-inspired gravity breaks it
item.description: Problem: In gravity theories with more than four dimensions, do different kinds of black-hole vibrations ring at the same frequency, and does string theory change that? Approach: Two mathematicians numerically computed the ringing frequencies of non-rotating black holes in 5-26 dimensions to 300 digits of precision, using a Chebyshev spectral method instead of standard approximations that fail on complex barrier shapes. Result: In plain Einstein gravity, scalar-field vibrations and spacetime-twist vibrations ring at identical frequencies - a hidden symmetry. Adding a string-theory correction (a Gauss-Bonnet term) breaks that symmetry immediately. Why it matters: It reveals hidden structure in Einstein's equations and shows where standard approximations fail, constraining theoretical models even though it's undetectable in real astronomical black holes. Glossary: Quasinormal modes - a black hole's characteristic ringing frequencies. Gauss-Bonnet term - a string-theory curvature correction to Einstein's equations. Chebyshev spectral method - a high-precision numerical technique. Supersymmetric quantum mechanics - a framework where paired equations share identical spectra.

item.title: AI-guided mutations help viruses infect bacteria up to 1 million times more effectively
item.description: Problem: Antibiotic resistance is outpacing new drug development, reviving interest in phage therapy - using viruses to kill bacteria - but natural phages often infect weakly or too broadly. Approach: University of Wisconsin-Madison researchers trained an AI model on tens of thousands of lab-measured phage protein mutations to predict which changes improve infection efficiency and narrow host targeting. Result: The model found mutations boosting bacterial-infection efficiency by up to a million-fold, while also identifying mutations that narrow a phage's targets to spare beneficial bacteria. Why it matters: Computationally guided phage engineering could speed up alternatives to failing antibiotics, for infections like UTIs, while protecting the gut microbiome. Glossary: Bacteriophage - a virus that infects bacteria. Phage therapy - treating infections with engineered viruses instead of antibiotics. Host specificity - a phage's ability to target only certain bacteria. High-throughput screening - lab testing of many genetic variants at once.

item.title: A 7-Segment Clock Built With No Digital Electronics
item.description: A 1970s-style clock displays digits using only a synchronous motor, gears, and sliding contacts - no digital logic at all.

item.title: Forging 1024-bit RSA signatures in nearly SNFS time
item.description: A new paper demonstrates forging 1024-bit RSA signatures in close to SNFS time, sharpening the case against short RSA moduli.

item.title: WaveDigger: Dig into wireless signals to discover their physical locations
item.description: An open-source tool maps wireless signal fingerprints back to physical locations, useful for geolocating devices without GPS.
